title: The Ruy Lopez
description: One of the oldest and most respected openings. White develops the bishop to b5, pressuring the knight that defends e5, and builds a lasting initiative.

sections.title: The Main Idea
sections.content: After 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5, White attacks the knight on c6 that defends the e5 pawn. The threat is not immediate, but the bishop creates long-term pressure on Black's center.

positions.commentary: The starting position of the Ruy Lopez. The bishop on b5 eyes the c6 knight. Black usually plays 3...a6 to question the bishop immediately.
hints: The Morphy Defense begins with a7-a6

sections.title: The Closed System
sections.content: In the Closed Ruy Lopez, both sides develop slowly and castle. White plays c3 and d4 to build a big center, while Black counters on the queenside. Patience and maneuvering define this opening.

positions.commentary: A typical Closed Ruy Lopez structure. White has retreated the bishop to b3 and castled. The slow battle for the center begins.

exercises.title: Maintain the Pressure
exercises.description: White to play. After ...a6, where does the bishop go to keep the pin alive?
